summary: When a woman finds she has become tamei, from when do the things she touched become tamei? Shammai, Hillel and the Sages each give a different answer.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
For all women, their own time is enough.
chunks.explain: Only things touched from the time she found it become tamei.

chunks.en: And Hillel says:
from one check to the next check,
chunks.explain: Everything she touched since she last checked becomes tamei.

words.note: A time she checked herself and found she was still tahor.

chunks.en: even for many days.
And the Sages say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one's words and not like that one's words,
but twenty-four hours makes it shorter

words.note: From this time yesterday until now: twenty-four hours.

chunks.en: than from check to check,
and from check to check makes it shorter
than twenty-four hours.
chunks.explain: We follow whichever time is shorter.

chunks.en: Any woman who has a set time,

words.note: A regular time when this tumah comes.

chunks.en: her own time is enough.
One who checks with cloths,

words.note: Cloths used to check whether she is tahor.

chunks.en: this counts like a check,
it makes it shorter than twenty-four hours
and than from check to check.

summary: How much dough must there be before we have to take challah from it? Shammai, Hillel and the Sages argue about the amount.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
from one kav, for challah.
chunks.explain: A kav is a measure of flour.

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: And Hillel says:
from two kavim. And the Sages say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one's words and not like that one's words,
but a kav and a half must have challah taken.
And when the measures were made bigger, they said:
five quarters must have challah taken.
Rabbi Yose says:
five quarters do not need it,
five and a little more must have it.

summary: How much drawn water ruins a mikveh? Hillel and Shammai argue, until two weavers came and told what Shemayah and Avtalyon had taught.

chunks.en: Hillel says:
a full hin of drawn water
chunks.explain: Water carried in a bucket, not water that came by itself.

words.note: A measure of liquid.

chunks.en: makes the mikveh not kosher;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁאָדָם חַיָּב לוֹמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹ.
chunks.en: he said hin only because a person must say it in his teacher's words.
And Shammai says:
nine kavim.
And the Sages say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one's words and not like that one's words,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁבָּאוּ שְׁנֵי גַרְדִּיִּים מִשַּׁעַר
chunks.en: but until two weavers came from the gate

chunks.he: הָאַשְׁפּוֹת שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְהֵעִידוּ מִשּׁוּם שְׁמַעְיָה וְאַבְטַלְיוֹן,
chunks.en: of the Dung Gate in Yerushalayim and testified in the name of Shemayah and Avtalyon:

words.note: The name of one of the gates of Yerushalayim.
The teachers of Shammai and Hillel.

chunks.en: three lugin of drawn water

words.note: A small measure of liquid.

chunks.en: make the mikveh not kosher,
and the Sages accepted their words.

summary: Why does the Mishnah tell us what Shammai and Hillel said, if we do not follow them? To teach that a person should not hold on stubbornly to his opinion.

chunks.en: And why do we mention the words
of Shammai and Hillel for nothing?
To teach the future generations that a person
should not stand firm on his words,
since the fathers of the world did not

words.note: Great leaders, like Shammai and Hillel.

chunks.en: stand firm on their words.

summary: Why does the Mishnah tell us the opinion of one Sage when the halachah follows the many? So that a later beis din can rely on it.

chunks.he: וְלָמָּה מַזְכִּירִין דִּבְרֵי הַיָּחִיד בֵּין הַמְרֻבִּין,
chunks.en: And why do we mention the words of one person among the many,

chunks.he: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין הֲלָכָה אֶלָּא כְדִבְרֵי הַמְרֻבִּין.
chunks.en: since the halachah is only like the words of the many?
So that if a beis din sees

words.note: A court of Torah judges.

chunks.en: the words of the one and relies on him.
For a beis din cannot cancel
the words of another beis din unless
it is greater than it in wisdom and in number.
If it was greater than it in wisdom
but not in number,
in number but not in wisdom,
it cannot cancel its words,

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גָדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ בְחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן:
chunks.en: unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number.

summary: Rabbi Yehudah gives another reason for writing down the opinion of one Sage: so that if someone says "this is what I was taught," we can tell him it was only that Sage's opinion.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said:
If so, why do we mention the words
of the one among the many for nothing?

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם יֹאמַר הָאָדָם כָּךְ אֲנִי מְקֻבָּל,
chunks.en: So that if a person says, "This is what I was taught,"
we can say to him:
"You heard it as the words of So-and-so."

summary: How many bones of a dead person make a tent tamei? Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel and Shammai each give an amount.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
a quarter-kav of bones from the bones,
chunks.explain: This much makes things in the same tent tamei.

chunks.en: whether from two or from three people.
And Beis Hillel say:
a quarter-kav of bones from one body,
from most of the frame or most of the number of bones.
Shammai says:
even from one bone.

summary: Karshinim are a kind of bean usually fed to animals. If they are terumah, how careful must we be to keep them tahor?

chunks.en: Karshinim of terumah,

words.note: A kind of bean, mostly fed to animals.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
we soak them and rub them while staying tahor,
and we feed them to animals even while tamei.
Beis Hillel say:
we soak them while staying tahor,
and we rub and feed them even while tamei.
Shammai says:
they should be eaten dry.
Rabbi Akiva says:
everything done with them may be done while tamei.

summary: Someone changes a big coin of maaser sheni money into smaller coins. How much of it may he change into copper coins?

chunks.en: One who changes a sela of maaser sheni money,
chunks.explain: Money used to buy food to eat in Yerushalayim.

words.note: A big silver coin.
A tenth of the crops.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
for the whole sela, copper coins.
And Beis Hillel say:
for a shekel of silver and a shekel of copper coins.

words.note: Half a sela.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין כֶּסֶף וּפֵרוֹת עַל הַכֶּסֶף.
chunks.en: we do not switch silver and fruit onto silver.
And the Sages allow it.

summary: Now someone changes a sela of maaser sheni money in Yerushalayim. How much may he change into copper coins to spend there?

chunks.he: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
chunks.en: One who changes a sela of maaser sheni in Yerushalayim,
Beis Shammai say:
for the whole sela, copper coins.
And Beis Hillel say:
for a shekel of silver and a shekel of copper coins.
Those who argued before the Sages say:
for three dinars of silver and one dinar of copper coins.

words.note: Silver coins; four make a sela.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
for three dinars of silver, and for a quarter
of silver, a quarter in copper coins.
And Rabbi Tarfon says:
four silver aspers.

words.note: Small silver coins.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
he should leave it in the shop and eat its worth.

summary: A bride's chair or a seat built onto a kneading trough: can they become tamei? Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue.

chunks.en: A bride's chair whose covers were taken off,
Beis Shammai say it can become tamei,
and Beis Hillel say it stays tahor.
Shammai says:
even the frame of a chair can become tamei.
A seat that was fixed onto a kneading trough,
Beis Shammai say it can become tamei,
and Beis Hillel say it stays tahor.
Shammai says:
even one made as part of it.

summary: Beis Hillel changed their minds to teach like Beis Shammai. If a woman comes from far away and says her husband died, she may marry again and also collect her kesubah.

chunks.en: These are things where Beis Hillel went back
to teach like the words of Beis Shammai.
A woman who came from a faraway land

words.note: A faraway country.

chunks.en: and said, "My husband died,"
may marry again. "My husband died,"
she may do yibum. And Beis Hillel say:
We only heard this about one who came
from the harvest alone.
Beis Shammai said to them:

chunks.he: אַחַת הַבָּאָה מִן הַקָּצִיר וְאַחַת הַבָּאָה
chunks.en: It is the same if she came from the harvest, or came

chunks.he: מִן הַזֵּיתִים וְאַחַת הַבָּאָה מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: from the olives, or came from a faraway land;
they spoke of the harvest only because that is what happened.

chunks.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמָּאי.
chunks.en: Beis Hillel went back to teach like Beis Shammai.
Beis Shammai say:
she may marry and take her kesubah.

words.note: The money a husband promises his wife.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
she may marry but not take her kesubah.
Beis Shammai said to them:
You allowed the strict thing, a forbidden marriage,
will you not allow the easy thing, money?
Beis Hillel said to them:
We find that the brothers do not come in
to the inheritance because of her word.
Beis Shammai said to them:
But can we not learn from her kesubah paper,
where he writes to her:
"If you marry another man,
you take what is written for you."
Beis Hillel went back to teach
like the words of Beis Shammai.

summary: A man who is half a slave and half free cannot marry anyone. Beis Shammai say his master must be made to free him, and Beis Hillel agreed.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: One who is half a slave and half free,
works for his master one day
and for himself one day,
these are the words of Beis Hillel.
Beis Shammai said to them:
You took care of his master,
but you did not take care of him.
To marry a maidservant,
he cannot.
A free woman,
he cannot.
Should he not marry? But the world was only created
for having children,
as it says (Yeshayahu 45):
"He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in."
Rather, to fix the world,

chunks.he: כּוֹפִין אֶת רַבּוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ בֶן
chunks.en: we force his master and he makes him

chunks.he: חוֹרִין וְכוֹתֵב שְׁטָר עַל חֲצִי דָמָיו.
chunks.en: free, and the slave writes a note for half his worth.

words.note: A paper saying he owes money.

chunks.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמָּאי:
chunks.en: Beis Hillel went back to teach like Beis Shammai.

summary: A sealed clay pot in a tent with a dead body keeps what is inside it tahor. What does it protect? Beis Hillel agreed with Beis Shammai.

chunks.en: A clay pot protects everything,
chunks.explain: If it is sealed and in a tent with a dead body.

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Hillel.
And Beis Shammai say:
it protects only foods
and drinks and clay vessels.
Beis Hillel said to them:
Why?
Beis Shammai said to them:
Because it is tamei on
account of an am ha'aretz,

words.note: A person who is not careful about tumah.

chunks.en: and a tamei vessel does not block.
Beis Hillel said to them:
But you said the foods and drinks in it are tahor!
Beis Shammai said to them:
When we said the foods and drinks in it are tahor,
we made them tahor only for him.
But when you make the vessel tahor,
you make it tahor for you and for him.
Beis Hillel went back to teach
like the words of Beis Shammai.
